Environmental Time Series Plot

Source: R/plotting.R
series_plot.Rd

Creates time-series plots for environmental monitoring data.

Usage

series_plot(df, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
series_plot(
  df,
  location,
  sample_date,
  analyte,
  result,
  unit = NULL,
  reporting_flag = NULL,
  reporting_limit = NULL,
  detection_limit = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'env_schema'
series_plot(
  df,
  result_col = analysis_result_var(df),
  scale = "free",
  scale_y_trans = "identity",
  trend = "none",
  trend_ci = FALSE,
  trend_conf_level = 0.95,
  trend_label = c("none", "compact", "full"),
  trend_label_sig_only = TRUE,
  background = NULL,
  standards = TRUE,
  short_name = FALSE,
  pnt = 3,
  ncol = NULL,
  plot_type = c("split", "combined"),
  ...
)

Arguments

df

A data frame or `env_schema` object.

...

Additional arguments passed to methods.

location

Location identifier column.

sample_date

Sample date column.

analyte

Analyte column.

result

Analytical result column.

unit

Reporting unit column.

reporting_flag

Reporting qualifier column.

reporting_limit

Reporting limit column.

detection_limit

Detection limit column.

scale

Facet scaling behavior passed to [ggplot2::facet_wrap()]. One of `"fixed"`, `"free"`, `"free_x"`, or `"free_y"`.

scale_y_trans

Transformation applied to the y-axis. One of `"identity"`, `"log"`, `"log10"`, `"log2"`, `"log1p"`, `"sqrt"`, `"reverse"`, `"reciprocal"`, `"exp"`, `"boxcox"`, `"logit"`, `"probit"`, `"probability"`, `"atanh"`, or `"asn"`.

trend

Trend line method. One of `"none"`, `"lm"`, `"loess"`, `"gam"`, or `"mann_kendall"`.

trend_ci

Logical. If `TRUE`, confidence intervals are displayed for supported trend models.

trend_conf_level

Confidence level used when `trend_ci = TRUE`.

trend_label

Trend annotation format. One of `"none"`, `"compact"`, or `"full"`.

trend_label_sig_only

Logical. If `TRUE`, trend labels are displayed only for statistically significant trends.

background

Optional vector containing a start date and end date used to shade a background monitoring period.

standards

Logical. If `TRUE`, applicable analytical standards are displayed.

short_name

Logical. If `TRUE`, analyte titles use short analyte labels when available.

pnt

Point size for plotted observations.

ncol

Number of facet columns.

plot_type

Plot layout. One of `"split"` or `"combined"`.

Value

If `plot_type = "split"`, a named list of ggplot objects, one per analyte.

If `plot_type = "combined"`, a single ggplot object.

Details

`series_plot()` is an S3 generic that supports both raw data frames and `env_schema` objects.

For data frames, environmental column mappings must be supplied. For `env_schema` objects, mapped schema fields are used automatically.

For data frames, `series_plot()` first converts the supplied data to an `env_schema` object using the specified column mappings and then dispatches to [series_plot.env_schema()].

`series_plot()` produces time-series visualizations of environmental analytical results.

Data are grouped by analyte and location and displayed as chronological sampling records.

In `"split"` mode, a separate plot is created for each analyte. In `"combined"` mode, all analytes are displayed on a single plot using colour to distinguish analytes.

Non-detect observations are automatically distinguished from detected observations using symbol shape.

Optional trend lines, trend annotations, analytical standards, and background periods may be added to aid interpretation.

For `env_schema` objects, analyte, result, sample_date, unit, detection status, and location information are obtained directly from schema mappings and standardized analytical fields.

Plot Types

split

Produces a separate plot for each analyte.

combined

Produces a single plot containing all analytes with analytes distinguished by colour.

Trend Analysis

Several trend-fitting options are available:

none

No trend line is added.

lm

Linear regression trend.

loess

Locally weighted smooth trend.

gam

Generalized additive model smooth.

mann_kendall

Mann-Kendall trend test with associated annotation.

Detection Status

Detected and non-detect observations are displayed using different point symbols. Detection status is obtained from standardized censoring information contained in the `env_schema` object.

Schema-aware Plotting

For `env_schema` objects, `series_plot()` automatically uses:

  • the mapped sample_date field;

  • the mapped location field;

  • the mapped analyte field;

  • standardized analysis results;

  • standardized analysis units;

  • standardized censoring indicators.

This allows plots to be generated consistently regardless of original source column names.

Validation

Input arguments are validated for:

  • supported facet scaling options;

  • supported y-axis transformations;

  • supported trend-fitting methods;

  • presence of observations available for plotting.

Examples

data(gw)

plots <- series_plot(gw)

names(plots)
#>  [1] "Alkalinity, total (lab)"            "Aluminum, dissolved"
